Dear JE, 
Please join Katinka Matson and myself for the sixteenth annual EDGE dinner. The 
"Dinner" actually began 29 years ago at a Mexican restaurant during the 1985 
Comdex in Las Vegas as "The Millionaires' Dinner" (branded by the WSJ in a front 
page article). It became an annual event beginning in 1998 with our first dinner in 
Monterey, and then, in 2010, we moved it to Long Beach. It's been called "The 
Digerati Dinner", "The Billionaires' Dinner" (thanks to the WSJ again in 1999), 
"The EDGE Science Dinner", "The Last Digerati Dinner", and our favorite 
iteration, "The New Age of Wonder Dinner", characterized by Freeman Dyson as 
the new era dominated by computational biology. He said: 
"A new generation of artists, writing genomes as fluently as Blake and Byron wrote 
verses, might create an abundance of new flowers and fruit and trees and birds to 
enrich the ecology of our planet. Most of these artists would be amateurs, but they 
would be in close touch with science, like the poets of the earlier Age of Wonder. 
The new Age of Wonder might bring together wealthy entrepreneurs ... and a 
worldwide community of gardeners and farmers and breeders, working together to 
make the planet beautiful as well as fertile, hospitable to hummingbirds as well as 
to humans." 
"The leaders of the new Age of Wonder, Dyson noted, include 'biology wizards' Kary 
Mullis, Craig Venter, medical engineer Dean Kamen; and 'computer wizards' Larry 
Page, Sergey Brin, and Charles Simonyi, and John Brockman and Katinka 
Matson, the cofounders of EDGE, the nexus of this intellectual activity." 
See Dinner Albums at http://www.edge.orebillionairesdinner

Dear JE, 
Please join Katinka Matson and myself for the sixteenth annual EDGE dinner. The 
"Dinner" actually began 29 years ago at a Mexican restaurant during 
the 1985 Comdex in Las Vegas as "The Millionaires' Dinner" 
(branded by the WSJ in a front page article). It became an annual 
event beginning in 1998 with our first dinner in Monterey, and then, in 
I 0, we moved it to Long Beach. It's been called "The Digerati 
Dinner", "The Billionaires' Dinner" (thanks to the WSJ again in 1999), 
"The EDGE Science Dinner", "The Last Digerati Dinner", and our 
favorite iteration, "The New Age of Wonder Dinner", characterized 
by Freeman Dyson as the new era dominated by computational 
biology. He said: 
"A new generation of artists, writing genomes as fluently as Blake and Byron wrote 
verses, might create an abundance of new flowers and fruit and trees 
and birds to enrich the ecology of our planet. Most of these artists 
would be amateurs, but they would be in close touch with science, like 
the poets of the earlier Age of Wonder. The new Age of Wonder 
might bring together wealthy entrepreneurs ... and a worldwide 
community of gardeners and farmers and breeders, working together 
EFTA_R1_00734519 
EFTA02112134
--- PAGE 3 ---
to make the planet beautiful as well as fertile, hospitable to 
hummingbirds as well as to humans." 
"The leaders of the new Age of Wonder, Dyson noted, include 'biology wizards' 
Kart' Mullis, Craig Venter, medical engineer Dean Kamen; and 
'computer wizards' Larry Page, Sergey Brin, and Charles Simonyi, and 
John Brockman and Katinka Matson, the cofounders of EDGE, the 
nexus of this intellectual activity." 
See Dinner Albums at htto://www.edge.orgibillionaircsdinner

ABC Stone 
Background 
ABC Stone sponsored the 2013 Artist Residency in Carrara as part of its ongoing 
commitment to sustaining and promoting the use of stone in artistic practice. Of the 
many creative treatments of this material, traditional carving has suffered a decline of 
knowledge base during the past century. ABC seeks to address this by pairing young 
artists with master sculptors for experiential learning through intensive mentoring. It is 
our belief that deepening the awareness of stone commensurately widens respect for 
this venerable medium and the millennia-old human tradition in transforming it through 
highly skilled craft. Whether in Michelangelo's homeland or in our very own NYC 
backyard, ABC remains devoted to sponsoring the cultural arts and in particular stone 
artistry. 
Lisa Kirk 
Development Director

I have obtained the below from the website: www.cic.gc.ca (I called the Canadian 
Consulate in Washington—their message says to visit this website for the answers) 
Sweden: You do NOT need a Visa to visit or transit Canada. 
Poland: You DO need a Visa if you are a holder of a non-biometric passport only. 
If you are a holder of a biometric passport (e-passport) you do NOT need a visa. 
Belgium: You do NOT need a visa to visit or transit Canada. 
South African: You DO need a visa to visit or transit Canada. *Amex Centurian 
gave me the number to their visa services dept (www.visacentral.com/amex, 666 529 
6553) I was told if you have a Green Card and are going for business No visa is 
required. If you do not have a green card you must obtain a visa to visit or 
transit Canada*

Dear JE, 
Please join Katinka Matson and myself for the sixteenth annual EDGE dinner. The 
"Dinner" actually began 29 years ago at a Mexican restaurant during the 1985 
Comdex in Las Vegas as "The Millionaires' Dinner" (branded by the WSJ in a front 
page article). It became an annual event beginning in 1998 with our first dinner in 
Monterey, and then, in 2010, we moved it to Long Beach. It's been called "The 
Digerati Dinner", "The Billionaires' Dinner" (thanks to the WSJ again in 1999), 
"The EDGE Science Dinner", "The Last Digerati Dinner", and our favorite 
iteration, "The New Age of Wonder Dinner", characterized by Freeman Dyson as 
the new era dominated by computational biology. He said: 
"A new generation of artists, writing genomes as fluently as Blake and Byron wrote 
verses, might create an abundance of new flowers and fruit and trees and birds to 
enrich the ecology of our planet. Most of these artists would be amateurs, but they 
would be in close touch with science, like the poets of the earlier Age of Wonder. 
The new Age of Wonder might bring together wealthy entrepreneurs ... and a 
worldwide community of gardeners and farmers and breeders, working together to 
make the planet beautiful as well as fertile, hospitable to hummingbirds as well as 
to humans." 
"The leaders of the new Age of Wonder, Dyson noted, include biology wizards' Kary 
Mullis, Craig Venter, medical engineer Dean Kamen; and 'computer wizards' Larry 
Page, Sergey Brin, and Charles Simonyi, and John Brockman and Katinka 
Matson, the cofounders of EDGE, the nexus of this intellectual activity." 
See Dinner Albums at 
This year: Vancouver! Branding ("The xxxxx Dinner") to be inspired by the event and 
crowdsourced by our guests. While Katinka and I are not attending TED, we will 
be at the Fairmont Waterfront Hotel beginning Sunday, March 16th for the week, 
and we do want to see you. Can you join us? 
Time: 7:30 pm 
Date: Monday, March 17th 
Place: To Be Announced

Dear JE, 
Please join Katinka Matson and myself for the sixteenth annual EDGE dinner. The 
"Dinner" actually began 29 years ago at a Mexican restaurant during 
the 1985 Comdex in Las Vegas as "The Millionaires' Dinner" 
(branded by the WSJ in a front page article). It became an annual 
event beginning in 1998 with our first dinner in Monterey, and then, in 
2010, we moved it to Long Beach. It's been called "The Digerati 
Dinner", "The Billionaires' Dinner" (thanks to the WSJ again in 1999), 
"The EDGE Science Dinner", "The Last Digerati Dinner", and our 
favorite iteration, "The New Age of Wonder Dinner", characterized 
by Freeman Dyson as the new era dominated by computational 
biology. He said: 
"A new generation of artists, writing genomes as fluently as Blake and Byron wrote 
verses, might create an abundance of new flowers and fruit and trees 
EFTA_R1_00735697 
EFTA02112806
--- PAGE 3 ---
and birds to enrich the ecology of our planet. Most of these artists 
would be amateurs, but they would be in close touch with science, like 
the poets of the earlier Age of Wonder. The new Age of Wonder 
might bring together wealthy entrepreneurs ... and a worldwide 
community of gardeners and farmers and breeders, working together 
to make the planet beautiful as well as fertile, hospitable to 
hummingbirds as well as to humans." 
"The leaders of the new Age of Wonder, Dyson noted, include 'biology wizards' 
Kary Mullis, Craig Venter, medical engineer Dean Kamen; and 
'computer wizards' Larry Page, Sergey Brin, and Charles Simonyi, and 
John Brockman and Katinka Matson, the cofounders of EDGE, the 
nexus of this intellectual activity."
